pr_title: Make nudger and locomotor cache aware of temporary immovable units.
pr_body:
Follow-up to #17114 

Fixes #17117.

Even though deployed units cannot be nudged, they were still regarded as movable for the purpose of pathfinding and cascading nudges. This PR changes units with the mobile trait disabled or paused to be regarded as immovable.
pr_comments:
Update:
Divorced this logic from `RequireForceMove` so it also works correctly for deployable units that do not require alt to enable move orders.

issue_context.title: Nudging actors at production exits should check for success
issue_context.body:
If a nudge does not succeed, no new nudge is initiated, which can lead to exits being blocked by immobile actors even if there were other mobile actors than can be nudged.
Example:
![grafik](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7704140/65043286-eb54d480-d95a-11e9-88e2-b411b750eb2c.png)

Building two new tanks here has a good chance that the second tank will not exit the factory, since it most likely tires to nudge a deployed tick tank which in turn refuses to move. The unit will then not have space to exit although there are other actors that could be nudged.

review_comments: In some places we use Immobile and others Immovable. It would be good if we could standardize on one or the other (my preference would be Immobile).

The name was chosen to be consistent with the usage in `BlockedByActor.Immovable`, `CellFlag.HasMovableActor` and `CellCache.Immovable` among others. Those names where deliberately chosen to express a subtle difference in meaning with immobile: These categories also include actors that are quite mobile, but aren't movable by others (such as enemy units).

`Immobile` is actually only used as the name of a trait and nowhere else.
